subject: forensic-medicine
title: Legal Procedures: Police Inquest and Magistrate Inquest Framework

steps.title: Statutory concept and primary objectives of an inquest
steps.tx: In forensic jurisprudence, a formal **statutory inquest inquiry** represents a legal investigation conducted to ascertain the apparent cause of death in unnatural, sudden, suspicious, or violent fatalities. The investigating authority examines the dead body on-site, inspects the immediate surroundings, records witness statements, notes external injuries, and determines whether death resulted from homicide, suicide, accident, or natural disease under suspicious circumstances.
steps.say: An inquest is a legal inquiry into the cause of unnatural, sudden, or suspicious death. The investigating officer examines the deceased and surroundings to determine whether foul play occurred.

nodes.label: Discovery of unnatural or suspicious death
Intimation to local police or executive magistrate
On-site scene examination and panchnama
Requisition for medicolegal autopsy if indicated

steps.title: Police inquest under the criminal procedure framework
steps.tx: Governed by statutory criminal provisions, the **police inquest procedure** is initiated by the officer in charge of a police station or an authorized officer not below the rank of sub-inspector. Upon receiving information regarding an unnatural death, the investigating officer immediately proceeds to the scene, summons two or more respectable local inhabitants as panchas, inspects the deceased, and prepares a detailed panchnama report.
steps.say: Police inquests are conducted by a police sub-inspector who visits the scene, summons local witnesses called panchas, inspects the body, and writes a detailed panchnama report.

rows: Empowered under Section 174 CrPC / Section 194 BNSS
Must witness body inspection and sign panchnama report
Describes ligature marks, wounds, fractures and weapon marks
Mandatory whenever doubt exists regarding true cause of death

steps.tx: On news of an unnatural death the officer, not below a sub-inspector, goes to the place and calls at least two local residents as panchas. What they observe is written as a **panchnama** on Form 174, with the statutory header, columns for injuries, and the signatures of those panch witnesses. The paper describes the body and the scene. It is not a medical opinion, and it travels with the body to the doctor.
steps.say: The sub-inspector summons two or more panchas and writes Form 174. The form has a statutory header, columns for injuries and the panch signatures. It records the scene. It is not the postmortem opinion.

vis.alt: Police inquest Form 174 panchnama with a statutory header, injury columns and panch signatures.
vis.caption: Form 174 panchnama shows the statutory header, columns for injuries and the signatures of the panch witnesses. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: The inquest panchnama report and postmortem requisition
steps.tx: The formal **inquest panchnama document** describes the exact position of the deceased, clothing condition, postmortem staining distribution, rigor mortis, visible trauma, and ambient scene evidence. If any suspicion of foul play exists or the cause of death is not entirely obvious, the investigating officer forwards the corpse along with the inquest papers and dead body challan to the nearest authorized medical officer for autopsy.
steps.say: The panchnama describes the position of the body, clothing, lividity, wounds, and scene evidence. The officer sends these documents to the doctor with the autopsy requisition.

nodes.label: Scene inspection and documentation
Preparation of inquest report and challan
Secure body transport under police guard
Delivery to hospital mortuary for postmortem

steps.title: Magistrate inquest jurisdictions and statutory mandates
steps.tx: Under specialized circumstances, an authoritative **magistrate inquest inquiry** supersedes or supplements police inquiries to ensure judicial transparency and prevent administrative bias. Conducted by an Executive Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate, this inquiry is legally mandated in custodial deaths, deaths during police interrogation, deaths resulting from police firing, prison fatalities, and suspected dowry deaths occurring within seven years of marriage.
steps.say: Magistrate inquests are conducted by executive or judicial magistrates in custodial deaths, police firing, prison fatalities, and dowry deaths of women within seven years of marriage.

rows: Eliminates departmental bias and ensures independent judicial inquiry
Death of woman within 7 years of marriage
Screens for dowry homicide or coerced suicide under Section 304B
Determines legality of lethal force and crowd dispersal protocols
Provides lawful warrant for disinterment and medicolegal examination

steps.tx: A police panchnama is not enough when the state itself is under question. A **magistrate inquest** is held for a death in custody, during police questioning, from police firing, in prison, or a suspected dowry death within seven years of marriage. An executive magistrate conducts it. At the hospital mortuary the dead body challan accounts for the body from the ward to the autopsy table, so the chain is on paper before the first incision.
steps.say: An executive magistrate inquires into a custodial death, a death from police firing, a prison death, or a suspected dowry death within seven years of marriage. The dead body challan records the body at the mortuary.

vis.alt: Executive magistrate holding an inquest at a hospital mortuary, with the dead body challan.
vis.caption: An executive magistrate's inquest is under way at the mortuary, with the dead body challan beside the body. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Custodial deaths and judicial magistrate inquiry
steps.tx: To safeguard human rights, statutory law dictates that a **judicial magistrate custodial inquiry** must investigate every fatality occurring in police custody, judicial lock-up, or correctional institutions. The Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate personally visits the site, examines detention records, interviews fellow inmates, orders a videographed autopsy conducted by a medical board, and directly probes any allegations of physical torture or custodial violence.
steps.say: Every custodial death requires an inquiry by a judicial magistrate. The magistrate reviews detention logs, interviews inmates, and directs a videographed postmortem by a medical board.

nodes.label: Custodial death reported within 24 hours
Judicial magistrate visits detention cell
Videographed autopsy by medical board
Formal judicial finding submitted to rights commission

steps.title: Dowry deaths and Section 176 CrPC investigations
steps.tx: Whenever a woman dies within seven years of solemnization of marriage under unnatural circumstances, statutory provisions enforce a **mandatory dowry death inquest**. Conducted by a Sub-Divisional Magistrate or designated Executive Magistrate, this inquiry scrutinizes history of harassment, demand for valuable security, cruelty by the husband or in-laws, and directs an exhaustive medicolegal autopsy to establish whether death was homicidal or suicidal.
steps.say: Suspicious death of a woman within seven years of marriage demands an inquest by a sub-divisional magistrate. The magistrate investigates dowry harassment, cruelty, and cause of death.

right.title: Magistrate inquest
points: Conducted by executive or judicial magistrate
Mandatory in custodial and dowry deaths

steps.title: Exhumation procedures and magistrate warrants
steps.tx: When suspicion of foul play arises after burial, lawful **exhumation of buried human remains** can only proceed under a written warrant issued by an Executive Magistrate. The magistrate personally attends the disinterment at the gravesite, verifies the grave identity through gravediggers and relatives, oversees specimen collection of control soil samples above, beside, and below the coffin, and hands the corpse to forensic pathologists.
steps.say: Exhumation requires an order from an executive magistrate who attends the disinterment. Control earth samples are collected around the coffin to rule out environmental arsenic contamination.

nodes.label: Executive magistrate issues exhumation order

steps.title: Transition from Section 174 CrPC to Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita
steps.tx: In modern Indian criminal jurisprudence, traditional provisions have transitioned to the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita framework**, where Section 194 BNSS replaces the classic Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Similarly, Section 196 BNSS modernizes Section 176 CrPC magistrate inquiries, codifying strict timelines, promoting electronic documentation, integrating mandatory forensic videography, and harmonizing investigative duties across public mortuaries and magistrates.
steps.say: The new criminal code replaces section 174 CrPC with section 194 BNSS, and section 176 CrPC with section 196 BNSS, adding digital records and mandatory forensic videography.

rows: Power to summon witness to inquest
Inquiry by magistrate into cause of death

steps.title: Duties and clinical responsibilities of the autopsy surgeon
steps.tx: When receiving an inquest requisition, the official **autopsy surgeon verification duty** demands careful scrutiny of all enclosed police documents before commencing the postmortem examination. The medical officer cross-checks the dead body challan, verifies Constable identification marks, confirms police seals, matches alleged wound patterns against physical findings, and prepares an impartial, objective postmortem report for the presiding magistrate.
steps.say: The autopsy doctor must verify police seals, dead body challan details, and Constable identification before dissection, ensuring objective documentation for the court.

nodes.label: Verify police challan, constable badge and seals

Perform systematic complete three-cavity dissection
Preserve viscera and issue final autopsy report
